headline: Scientist World reports a benchmark of AI research agents across 1,000 executable paper environments
summary: A 5 November arXiv paper introduces Scientist World, which turns selected empirical papers into executable research environments. The authors report releasing 1,000 environments with reproduced baselines, hidden evaluation slices and separate verifier-agent checks. In their benchmark, agents improved on the reproduced method in 84% of improvement attempts and 74% of attempts that designed a method from scratch. The paper also reports raising Qwen3-8B’s median idea score across ten held-out papers after supervised fine-tuning and offline reinforcement learning; a fixed GPT-5.6 Sol implementer executed all ideas. These are author-reported results from the paper’s selected tasks and setup. They do not establish general autonomous scientific discovery, and were not independently audited or reproduced here. The linked project page shows zero indexed/analyzed/selected/future counters but elsewhere advertises 2,079 verified runs and a 76% result against the paper’s 74%. Public MIT system and CLI repositories are now visible; the linked environment organization shows no public repositories and the trace dataset returned HTTP 401. Access to the paper-specific environments/traces and the counter/score discrepancy remain unresolved.
